subject.title: refactor(nodes)!: retire arming leases for durable capability enablement

question: Should an upgrade remove the historical Phone Control deny seed and thereby treat an already locally enabled, pairing-approved node as durably authorized without the user re-enabling or re-approving it?
rationale: The code can implement either transition safely, but only maintainers can determine whether the old lease requirement represented a temporary implementation detail or a user-visible authorization promise that must survive upgrades.

options.title: Confirm durable-consent migration
options.body: Approve Doctor removal of the exact historical seed because node-local enablement plus pairing is the intended durable consent record, then require a real seeded-upgrade proof.

options.title: Preserve existing upgrade denials
options.body: Keep the historical deny entries for upgraded installations and make users opt into the new durable model through a deliberate enablement or migration action.

options.title: Split policy from retirement
options.body: Retire the lease plugin and journal now but defer the policy/default transition to a separately sponsored authorization decision.

recommendation.title: Confirm durable-consent migration
recommendation.body: Approve Doctor removal of the exact historical seed because node-local enablement plus pairing is the intended durable consent record, then require a real seeded-upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR body explicitly presents this authorization transition as a maintainer product decision and this person authored the proposed migration.
